doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: Synopsis must contain: title, abstract, introduction/background, problem statement, literature review, research gap, research questions or hypotheses, objectives, methodology, expected outcomes, ethical considerations, work plan/timeline and references.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: A synopsis should normally be 3,000 to 5,000 words (10 to 15 pages), double-spaced, 12-point font. The abstract must not exceed 300 words.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: The title must be specific, not exceed 20 words, and reflect the variables, population and context of the study. Overly broad titles are returned for revision.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: The problem statement must identify a clearly evidenced research gap supported by recent literature (preferably last five years) and explain why solving it matters.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: Objectives must be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound, use action verbs, and map one-to-one to the research questions or hypotheses.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: MS research should demonstrate sound application of existing methods to a defined problem. PhD research must show an original, publishable contribution to knowledge or theory.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: The methodology must justify the research design, define population and sampling technique with sample size justification, describe data collection instruments with validity and reliability evidence, and state the analysis techniques.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: All studies involving human participants, personal data or animals require approval of the Institutional Ethics Committee before data collection. Synopses must state informed consent and data confidentiality procedures.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: Total similarity must not exceed 19% and similarity from any single source must not exceed 5%, excluding references. A plagiarism report must accompany submission.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: A single recognised citation style (APA 7th, IEEE or as required by the department) must be used consistently. Every in-text citation must appear in the reference list and vice versa.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: A thesis must include title page, declaration, acknowledgements, abstract, table of contents, list of tables and figures, introduction, literature review, methodology, results, discussion, conclusion with recommendations, references and appendices.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: Thesis evaluation considers originality, rigor of methodology, quality of analysis, coherence between objectives and conclusions, writing quality, and at least one publication or submission for PhD candidates.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: The work plan must present realistic milestones. MS research should complete within 24 months and PhD within 36 to 48 months of registration, with semester-wise progress targets.

doc: Sample Graduate Handbook (generic - replace with your university's)
text: Writing must be formal, impersonal and concise. Avoid unsupported claims, long run-on sentences, and excessive passive voice. Technical terms must be defined at first use.
